newsitem.title: USA: Nat'l Presto cites cautious retail market.
newsitem.headline: Nat'l Presto cites cautious retail market.

text.p: National Presto Industries Inc on Friday attributed its weak third-quarter sales to a cautious retail environment and disappointing retailer acceptance of the company's 1996 new product introductions.
President Maryjo Cohen, in a statement, also cited "the general troubled state of the small appliance industry as well as a maturing product portfolio" as reasons for the lower sales.

For the September 29 third quarter, the appliance maker reported earnings of $2.8 million or $0.38 per share compared to $4.8 million or $0.65 per share a year ago. Sales fell to $23.0 million from $29.0 million.

National Presto said its 1995 third quarter included $2.3 million in pre-tax income from damages and interest resulting from Black & Decker Corp's infringement of the company's SaladShooter slicer/shredder patent. This was offset in part by the cost of retiring a convertible debenture issued in January 1991, Cohen said.
